You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Tech Giants Post Strong Earnings but Accelerated Spending Sparks Market Divergence; US-Iran Mutual Threats Push Up Oil Prices and Rate Hike Expectations; Gold and Silver Strengthen (July 23, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
US-Iran Tensions Drive Up Oil Prices, September Rate Hike Probability Nears 80%
U.S. President Trump threatened that if Iran fires on ships in the Strait of Hormuz—whether with missiles, rockets, drones, or other weapons—the United States will bomb and destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant. Iranian military sources responded that Iran has a firm will to exercise its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz and will never allow it to become a tool of threat against Iran again.
International crude oil futures settlement prices rose sharply, both hitting more than one-month highs. CME’s FedWatch Tool shows the probability of the Federal Reserve raising rates at least once before the end of its September meeting has approached 80%.
Market impact: Rising oil prices heighten inflation concerns and reinforce hawkish expectations, exerting short-term pressure on risk asset valuations while supporting the U.S. dollar and gold as safe-haven assets.
International Commodities
Crude Oil Surges on Geopolitical Risks, Precious Metals Strengthen in Tandem
Stimulated by mutual threats between the U.S. and Iran, both WTI and Brent crude oil closed significantly higher.
Spot gold and silver rose on the back of safe-haven demand and a slightly weaker U.S. dollar.
Market impact: Higher energy costs may pass through to downstream prices, increasing uncertainty around the Fed’s policy path and keeping commodity market volatility elevated.
Macroeconomic Policy
Trump Warns of Possible Government Shutdown in September; Bank of Japan Open to Faster Rate Hikes
Speaking in Georgia, President Trump stated that due to differences between Republicans and Democrats on spending priorities, a federal government shutdown is expected in September. The Republican-controlled House has passed a short-term funding bill extending government funding through December 4; the Senate is still negotiating.
Informed sources indicate that the continued weakness of the yen has heightened upside risks to inflation, and Bank of Japan officials are open to raising rates at a faster pace than economists generally expect. Markets widely anticipate the BOJ will keep rates unchanged at its July 31 meeting.
Market impact: Rising U.S. fiscal uncertainty and greater policy flexibility from the BOJ may increase volatility in global capital flows, providing short-term support for the safe-haven attributes of U.S. dollar assets.
II. Market Review
Commodities Forex Performance
Spot Gold : $4,130.99/oz, -0.02%
Spot Silver : $59.72/oz, +0.08%
WTI Crude Oil : Approx. $87.9/barrel, +1.21%
Brent Crude Oil : Approx. $95.55/barrel, +1.57%
U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) : 101.09, -0.03%
Driver Analysis : U.S.-Iran tensions directly pushed crude oil higher, with traders concerned that rising energy prices will lift consumer goods inflation and thereby reinforce expectations of a September Fed rate hike. Gold and silver benefited from geopolitical safe-haven demand and a slightly weaker dollar, rising in tandem. In the near term, if tensions in the Strait of Hormuz persist, oil prices are likely to remain elevated and further suppress risk appetite; if tensions ease, commodity gains could reverse quickly. Institutions generally view current commodity markets as highly sensitive to geopolitical risk premiums and are closely monitoring subsequent U.S. and Iranian statements.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approx. $66,199, -0.66%
ETH : Approx. $1,937, -0.03%
Total Crypto Market Cap : Approx. $2.33 trillion, -0.5%
Market Liquidations : 24h total liquidations approx. $183 million, of which long liquidations $106 million
Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map : Current price around $66,153. Significant short liquidation clusters are concentrated in the $66,700–$67,500 range above; a break above $66,500 could trigger cascading short covering and accelerate short-term upside. Long liquidation pressure below is mainly concentrated in the $65,300–$64,500 zone but is weaker than overhead, so the current liquidation structure still leans toward sweeping short liquidity first.
Spot ETF Net Flows : BTC spot ETFs recorded net inflows of approx. $203 million yesterday; current 24-hour dynamic net inflow stands at $30 million, marking the 7th consecutive day of net inflows.

Performance Summary Driver Analysis : The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 0.44% against the broader market, led by Nvidia and Broadcom, reflecting continued strong demand for AI infrastructure. In contrast, software and application software stocks weakened notably, with Palantir falling more than 6% and Salesforce more than 4%. Although Alphabet and Tesla reported strong revenue in their after-hours earnings, the substantial upward revisions to capital expenditure guidance and the shift to negative free cash flow sparked market concerns about the pace of “spending acceleration,” resulting in sharp stock divergence. Overall, the sector showed a clear split between AI hardware beneficiaries and pressure on software and certain consumer electronics names, with valuation and cash-flow quality becoming the core factors for re-pricing by investors.
[...]
Representative stocks: Nvidia +2.3%, Broadcom +2.67%
[...]
1. Alphabet – Cloud Business Exceeds Expectations but Free Cash Flow Turns Negative for the First Time Event Overview : Q2 revenue and earnings both exceeded expectations, with Google Cloud delivering its strongest growth in recent quarters and a backlog of $51.4 billion. The company raised full-year capital expenditure guidance to $195–205 billion to accelerate AI compute expansion. Free cash flow turned negative for the first time in the company’s history, and shares fell more than 3% in after-hours trading. Market Interpretation : Institutions acknowledge the progress in cloud and AI monetization but remain cautious about the large upward revision to capex and the deterioration in cash flow, concerned that the payback period may lengthen. Investment Implication : The AI investment race has entered a white-hot phase; cash-flow quality is becoming a key pricing factor for the next stage.
[...]
2. Tesla – Revenue Beats Expectations but Profits Disappoint; Cash Flow Turns Negative Event Overview : Q2 revenue reached $28.236 billion, up 26% year-over-year and above the market expectation of $25.71 billion; automotive revenue was $20.516 billion. Profits missed due to lower average selling prices and promotional activity. Capital expenditure fell short of targets and free cash flow turned negative. Management emphasized that the company is in its largest investment phase. Market Interpretation : Strong deliveries were well received, but margin and cash-flow pressure have prompted investors to reassess the pace of investment in robotics and autonomous driving. Investment Implication : Balancing volume growth with profitability remains the core challenge; subsequent gross-margin recovery will be closely watched.
[...]
Alphabet (Google’s parent) reported Q2 2026 results on July 22. Revenue reached $119.8 billion, up 24% year-over-year—the 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth and above expectations. GAAP operating income was $40.8 billion, up 30%, with operating margin expanding to 34%. GAAP EPS of $9.11 exceeded consensus. Net income was significantly boosted by investment gains, including fair-value changes in certain equity investments.
[...]
Tesla left its Bitcoin holdings unchanged in Q2 at 11,509 BTC, extending a nearly four-year period with no buys or sells. Affected by Bitcoin’s decline from approximately $83,000 to $58,000 during the quarter, Tesla recorded a $112 million after-tax impairment loss on its digital asset holdings.
